clue.text: Each sovereign of 1690 only worth so much?

definitions.text: Each sovereign of 1690 only worth so much?

parts.words: Each sovereign of 1690 only worth so much?
parts.note: in 1690 two rival kings, William III and James II, fought at the Boyne over one throne, so each had only part of the royal headgear; the coin of that name puns on this

explanation.surface: A question about what the coins of a seventeenth-century monarch were worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like the gold coin but means a king. A half-crown was an old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both an old British coin and a punning picture of two kings sharing one throne.

clue.text: Worker's cards

definitions.meaning: the set of cards a player holds in a game

explanation.definitionFit: A labourer is a hand on a farm or ship, and the cards dealt to one player form a hand.

clue.text: Chain, say, a wild-cat

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken and we want a different spelling of the same sound

parts.note: a chain is made of links

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark comparing a chain with a wild animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a short-tailed wild feline with tufted ears.

clue.text: To address thus is, perhaps, too contrived

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone worries that addressing a person this way is rather too artificial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge but is fodder along with 'is' and 'too'; 'contrived' signals the rearrangement. Apostrophising means addressing someone absent, as in 'O Death!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To apostrophise is to address an absent person or thing directly in rhetoric.

clue.text: Reach maturity in State Penitentiary

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a pen is slang for a penitentiary, a prison

explanation.surface: A prisoner grows up while serving time in an American state jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit or people mature when they ripen, coming to full development.

clue.text: Rode like a highwayman, for example

parts.note: the word rode is the word doer with its letters set out wrongly

explanation.surface: Describes someone riding as a highwayman would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rode' looks like the past tense of ride, but it is the letters of DOER in the wrong order.
explanation.definitionFit: A highwayman robbed travellers, so he is a criminal, one who commits offences.

clue.text: Specialist holds back non-professional

indicators.note: back means the hidden run is read in reverse order
holds means the word Specialist contains the run we want inside it

explanation.surface: An expert keeps an amateur in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds' finds CIAL inside 'Specialist'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, belonging to the laity rather than to a profession or the clergy.

clue.text: Like Jimmy Porter, getting Archie into trouble

indicators.note: getting into trouble means these letters are put into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Archie gets into a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like part of 'getting into trouble' but is fodder with 'Archie'. Jimmy Porter is the angry hero of John Osborne's 1956 play Look Back in Anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Porter is the classic angry young man lacking traditional heroic virtues, an archetypal protagonist of that type.

clue.text: Match without a hard spell of bowling to fathom

indicators.note: without means the letter a is taken away from the word before

parts.note: to match two things is to compare them
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
in cricket a bowler bowls a spell from one end of the pitch

explanation.surface: A cricket match with no long hard spell of bowling, which one tries to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom something is to understand it fully, to grasp it.

clue.text: No income? Poor Pa is neverending fool

indicators.note: never-ending means each of these words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A family with no money and a feckless father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neverending' cuts the final letter from No, income, Poor and Pa, leaving N, INCOM, POO and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a silly person, an idiot.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of red or white rose

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow of blood is to stop it

definitions.text: supporter of red or white rose
definitions.meaning: the stalk that holds up a flower

explanation.definitionFit: To staunch bleeding is to check it, and a rose's stalk holds up the bloom.

clue.text: Tax-collector holds party for peasant

indicators.note: holds means the first word contains the second inside it

parts.note: a tax farmer historically bought the right to collect taxes
Labour is a British political party

explanation.surface: A tax official hosts a celebration for a poor villager.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a rural worker of the land, a field hand.

clue.text: Office worker gets her apron twisted

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A secretary's apron gets caught up and crumpled.
explanation.definitionFit: A stenographer writes shorthand, typically employed as a secretary or typist.

clue.text: Theatre joint — quiet party put up the capital

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
P stands for piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A dodgy joint where a quiet party is set up in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippodrome is a name for a music hall or theatre, from the Greek word for a racecourse.

clue.text: Temperate Jack has 10 notes from debtors

parts.note: jack and AB are both words for a sailor (able seaman)
the answer to 10 across
an IOU is a note of debt

explanation.surface: Jack holds ten notes of debt from people who owe him.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious means moderate in eating and drinking, self-restrained.

clue.text: Fifty in one big room, milling about in confusion

indicators.note: in means the letter for fifty goes inside the rearranged letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: milling about means moving around aimlessly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people milling about in one large room in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milling about' rearranges the letters, with 'one' giving I as a Roman numeral; 'in' places the fifty inside. 'In confusion' looks like the anagram signal, but 'confusion' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a complicated, embarrassing tangle or muddle.

clue.text: Feature me in a row with worker

parts.note: a row is a line

indicators.note: in means the word me goes inside the word for worker

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stands in a queue alongside a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineaments are the distinctive features of a face or body.

clue.text: Boundary beginning on the left

definitions.meaning: a ... is a border region, as in the Welsh ...
a soldier sets off on parade stepping off with the left foot

explanation.definitionFit: A border territory is a march, and to set off as soldiers do, left foot first, is to march.

clue.text: Throw in a diamond, or play high with club

definitions.meaning: to throw the ball to the batter on a baseball diamond
a golf shot lofting the ball high onto the green

explanation.definitionFit: A baseball pitcher throws to the batter, and a golfer lofts a short shot to the green in the same word.

clue.text: Telling how top sailor managed to return

indicators.note: to return means everything is read back to front

parts.note: number one, written NO I, is the top
a tar is a sailor
ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: An account of how a leading seaman got back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To return' turns the whole run NOITARRAN backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A narration is the act of telling a story, an account.

clue.text: Ordered by a king, do some do record work?

definitions.text: Ordered by a king, do some do record work?

parts.words: Ordered by a king, do some do record work?
parts.note: William the Conqueror ordered a great survey of land in 1086; the question reads its title as a day spent doing record work

explanation.surface: Asks whether some people at a king's command do clerical recording.
explanation.walkthrough: The Domesday Book was the 1086 survey of England commissioned by William I.
explanation.definitionFit: The great English survey compiled for William the Conqueror is that record.

clue.text: Troops with it are suitable

parts.note: BEF is the British Expeditionary Force, troops sent to France in both world wars

explanation.surface: Soldiers who have the right stuff are fit for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be appropriate for, so things that befit are fitting.

clue.text: Liberal I know, in speech -—- on the floor of the House?

definitions.text: on the floor of the House?

indicators.note: in speech means the next word is spoken and we need a word that sounds the same

parts.note: know is pronounced the same as no

explanation.surface: A Liberal MP declares his knowledge in a speech in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The floor of the House' sounds like the Commons chamber but means a floor in a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Linoleum is a floor covering laid in houses.

clue.text: Times shows annual increase

explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long periods, and someone getting a year older each birthday grows older.

clue.text: Musician gets honour without love

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the honour goes round the letter for love

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A performer receives a decoration but no affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside'. The definition names the player by the instrument, as orchestras do.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra's woodwind player can be called by the instrument, like first violin.

clue.text: Acting by, and on behalf of, China

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
for means on behalf of
Ming is a Chinese dynasty, famous for its porcelain

explanation.surface: Someone acting both through and for China.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on stage means giving a show, putting on a play.

clue.text: Commit robbery with no difficulty

definitions.meaning: to relieve someone of property, humorously, as in easing him of his wallet
the absence of effort, as in doing it with facility

explanation.definitionFit: Easing a man of his purse is jocular for robbing him, and freedom from effort is facility.

clue.text: Gallery has space in ship for cabins

indicators.note: in means the gallery and space go inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the Tate is a famous London art gallery
room means space

explanation.surface: An art gallery has room aboard a vessel for passenger berths.
explanation.definitionFit: Staterooms are private passenger cabins on a ship.
